correctness.rationale: For the repaired result only: the frozen closure table and prose say a singleton entering a size-two row of (2^p,1) yields (3,2^p), which has the wrong total n; the correct result is (3,2^(p−1)). For example (2,2,2,1) becomes (3,2,2) at n=7. When p=1 and there are at least two singleton rows the same donor/recipient type produces the hook (3,1^(q−1)), not listed in the frozen explanatory subcases. At (3,1), the move from size 3 to size 1 gives (2,2), contrary to the frozen blanket statement that other nontrivial outcomes have at least three sizes. A fresh-row move from the larger part of (a,b) gives the equal-largest odd exception only for a=b+1 and b>=2, since b=1,a=2 yields support one. The replacement proof treats all feasible donor/recipient sizes with multiplicity checks and filters loops and support-one/three results. A transfer is reversible by moving a unit back, creating a fresh row if the old donor was a singleton, so enumerating outgoing transfers suffices for undirected closure. From H only H,T,U survive; T gives T,H, or (b,b,1); U gives U,H, or (3,2^(p−1)). The two extra families attach by one edge to their respective chains and are adjacent to each other only for n=7. At n=5 the would-be extras already lie in U_5 and T_5, and n=3 is a singleton. For n>=4 the only intersections of H,T,U are the two different end hooks. Inclusion–exclusion and the two distinct odd added vertices give the stated orders. The witness (n−4,2,2) is two-support outside the closed set for every n>=8; whole-stratum counts for n=3..7 are 1,2,5,6,11. Independent indexed-row BFS with all partitions confirmed the component at n=3..24 and agreed with the value-pair implementation on all support-two vertices at these sizes; feasible value-pair closure was checked through n=250. This preserves the theorem statement but corrects a false exhaustive description in the supporting proof.
residual_risks: The finite BFS and closure replays stop at different bounds. The corrected case analysis, not either bounded experiment, is the all-n proof. There is no claim about the membership of other components.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The known paths give the connected base family (after omitting the support-one endpoints), and the general multiplicity rule is a known ingredient. value.rationale: This is a natural distinguished component of the smallest nontrivial support stratum of an established transfer graph. The exact closure and odd exceptions describe which boundary configurations communicate; the order and witness turn a short computational connectivity observation into a sharp theorem for all n in this stratum. The value is not the three known paths or an exhaustive census of every component. Repairing the transfer proof keeps that substantive structural content unchanged.
residual_risks: No broader value claim for higher support, the full graph or the other components.
